english_text: Antiretroviral therapy should be started as soon as possible after an HIV diagnosis.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (Antiretroviral therapy) e lokela ho qaleha kapele kamoo ho ka khonehang ka mor'a ho fumanoa u ena le tšoaetso ea HIV.

english_text: All people living with HIV should receive antiretroviral therapy regardless of their CD4 count.
sesotho_text: Batho bohle ba phelang le tšoaetso ea HIV ba lokela ho fumana phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (antiretroviral therapy) ho sa tsotellehe boemo ba lisele tsa bona tsa tšireletso tsa CD4 (CD4 count).

english_text: Starting ART early reduces the risk of serious illness and death.
sesotho_text: Ho qala phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) kapele ho fokotsa kotsi ea ho kula haholo le lefu.

english_text: Your doctor will choose the best ART regimen based on your health and other medicines you take.
sesotho_text: Ngaka ea hau e tla khetha moralo o motle oa phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART regimen) ho latela bophelo ba hau le meriana e meng eo u e nwang.

english_text: ART does not cure HIV but it controls the virus and protects your immune system.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ha e phekole HIV ho e qeta, empa e laola kokwanahloko le ho ts'ireletsa sesole sa mmele sa hau.

english_text: You must take ART every day for the rest of your life.
sesotho_text: U lokela ho nwa phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) letsatsi le leng le le leng bophelo bohle ba hau.

english_text: Missing doses of ART can cause the virus to become resistant to treatment.
sesotho_text: Ho tlola meriana ea phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ho ka etsa hore kokwanahloko e rutehe 'me e tloaele moriana, ebe e thibela phekolo ho sebetsa (treatment resistance).

english_text: Taking ART at the same time every day helps maintain the right level of medicine in your blood.
sesotho_text: Ho nwa phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ka nako e tšoanang letsatsi le leng le le leng ho thusa ho boloka boemo bo nepahetseng ba moriana maling a hau.

english_text: ART reduces the amount of HIV in your blood to very low levels.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) e fokotsa bongata ba kokwanahloko ea HIV maling a hau ho fihla maemong a tlase haholo.

english_text: People on ART can live long and healthy lives.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang ka phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ba ka phela bophelo bo bolelele le bo nang le bophelo bo botle.

english_text: ART protects your immune system by keeping your CD4 count high.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) e ts'ireletsa sesole sa mmele sa hau ka ho boloka boemo ba lisele tsa CD4 bo phahame.

english_text: The goal of ART is to make the viral load undetectable in your blood.
sesotho_text: Sepheo sa phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ke ho etsa hore bongata ba kokwanahloko (viral load) bo fokotsehe hoo bo ke keng ba hlola bo bonahala maling a hau (undetectable).

english_text: An undetectable viral load means the treatment is working.
sesotho_text: Bongata ba kokwanahloko bo sa hloleng bo bonahala (undetectable viral load) bo bolela hore phekolo e ntse e sebetsa hantle.

english_text: Do not stop taking your ART even if you feel healthy.
sesotho_text: U se ke ua tlohela ho nwa phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) leha u ikutloa u phetse hantle e bile u le matla.

english_text: Tell your healthcare provider if you have difficulty taking your medicines every day.
sesotho_text: Polella mofani oa hau oa tlhokomelo ea bophelo (ngaka kapa moki) haeba u na le bothata ba ho nwa meriana ea hau letsatsi le leng le le leng.

english_text: A pill organiser can help you remember to take your medicines on time.
sesotho_text: "Sehlophisi sa lipilisi (pill organiser) se ka u thusa ho hopola ho nwa meriana ea hau ka nako e nepahetseng.

english_text: Setting a daily alarm can help you remember to take your HIV medicine.
sesotho_text: Ho jala alamo ea letsatsi le leng le le leng ho ka u thusa ho hopola ho nwa moriana oa hau oa HIV.

english_text: Ask a trusted friend or family member to help remind you to take your medicine.
sesotho_text: Kopa motsoalle kapa setho sa lelapa seo u se tšepang ho u hopotsa ho nwa moriana oa hau.

english_text: Your pharmacist can answer questions about your HIV medicines.
sesotho_text: Rematanyane kapa ralechesi oa hau (pharmacist) a ka araba lipotso mabapi le meriana ea hau ea HIV.

english_text: Always collect your ART refill before you run out of medicine.
sesotho_text: Kogela kapa u khee letsoho la phekolo ea hau ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) kamehla pele meriana eo u nang le eona e fela.

english_text: A CD4 count measures the number of CD4 cells in your blood.
sesotho_text: Palo ea CD4 (CD4 count) e lekanya bongata ba lisele tsa CD4 maling a hau.

english_text: A normal CD4 count is between 500 and 1500 cells per cubic millimetre.
sesotho_text: Palo e tloaelehileng ea CD4 e lipakeng tsa lisele tse 500 le 1500 khubiki milimitara ka 'ngoe (cells per cubic millimetre).

english_text: A CD4 count below 200 means your immune system is severely weakened.
sesotho_text: Palo ea CD4 e ka tlase ho lisele tse 200 e bolela hore sesole sa mmele sa hau se fokola haholo.

english_text: Your CD4 count should be checked regularly when you start ART.
sesotho_text: Palo ea lisele tsa hau tsa CD4 e lokela ho hlahlojoa kamehla ka mor'a hore u qale phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART).

english_text: A rising CD4 count means your immune system is recovering on ART.
sesotho_text: Palo e ntseng e phahama ea CD4 e bolela hore sesole sa mmele sa hau se ntse se hlaphoheloa ka lebaka la phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART).

english_text: Viral load testing measures how much HIV is in your blood.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea bongata ba kokwanahloko (viral load testing) e lekanya hore na ho na le HIV e kae maling a hau.

english_text: A viral load below 200 copies per millilitre is considered suppressed.
sesotho_text: Bongata ba kokwanahloko bo ka tlase ho likopi tse 200 mililitara ka 'ngoe (200 copies per millilitre) bo nkoa bo hatelitsoe kapa bo le tlas'a taolo (suppressed).

english_text: Viral load should be tested six months after starting ART.
sesotho_text: Bongata ba kokwanahloko (viral load) bo lokela ho hlahlojoa likhoeli tse tšeletseng ka mor'a hore u qale phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART).

english_text: A high viral load means the virus is not well controlled.
sesotho_text: Bongata bo phahameng ba kokwanahloko (high viral load) bo bolela hore vaerase ha ea laoleha hantle.

english_text: Regular monitoring helps your doctor know if your ART is working.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea madi ea ho beha leihlo lebelo la HIV (HIV monitoring) hangata e etsoa kamora likhoeli tse ling le tse ling tse tharo ho isa ho tse tšeletseng.

english_text: Blood tests for HIV monitoring are usually done every three to six months.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea madi ea ho beha leihlo lebelo la HIV (HIV monitoring) hangata e etsoa kamora likhoeli tse ling le tse ling tse tharo ho isa ho tse tšeletseng.

english_text: Keep all your laboratory appointments even if you feel well.
sesotho_text: Boloka lipehelo (appointments) tsohle tsa hau tsa laboratoring leha u ikutloa u phetse hantle.

english_text: Ask your healthcare provider to explain your test results to you.
sesotho_text: Kōpa mofani oa hau oa litšebeletso tsa bophelo (healthcare provider) ho u hlalosetsa liphetho tsa hau tsa tlhahlobo.

english_text: A falling CD4 count may mean your treatment needs to be changed.
sesotho_text: Palo e ntseng e theoha ea CD4 e ka bolela hore phekolo ea hau e hloka ho fetoloa.

english_text: Viral load testing is the best way to know if ART is working.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea bongata ba kokwanahloko (viral load testing) ke tsela e molemohali ea ho tseba hore na phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) e ntse e sebetsa hantle.

english_text: Some HIV medicines can cause nausea especially when you first start taking them.
sesotho_text: Meriana e meng ea HIV e ka baka ho nyekeloa ke pelo (nausea), haholo-holo ha u qala ho e nka.

english_text: Taking ART with food can help reduce nausea.
sesotho_text: Ho nka phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) le lijo ho ka thusa ho fokotsa ho nyekeloa ke pelo (nausea).

english_text: Some ART medicines can cause dizziness or headache in the first few weeks.
sesotho_text: Meriana e meng ea ART e ka baka ho tsekela kapa ho tšoaroa ke hlooho (dizziness or headache) libekeng tse seng kae tsa pele.

english_text: Tell your doctor immediately if you develop a severe rash after starting ART.
sesotho_text: Prisang mofani oa hau oa bophelo kapa ngaka kapele-pele haeba u e-ba le lekhopho le matla (severe rash) ka mor'a ho qala phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART).

english_text: Some HIV medicines can affect your liver and regular liver tests may be needed.
sesotho_text: Meriana e meng ea HIV e ka ama sebete sa hau, 'me ho ka hlokahala hore u etse litlhahlobo tsa kamehla tsa sebete (regular liver tests).

english_text: Fatigue is a common side effect when starting ART and usually improves over time.
sesotho_text: Mokhathala (fatigue) ke phello e tloaelehileng ea lehlakore ha u qala phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART), 'me hangata o ntlafala ha nako e ntse e ea.

english_text: Some ART medicines can cause vivid dreams or difficulty sleeping.
sesotho_text: Meriana e meng ea ART e ka baka litoro tse hlakileng haholo kapa bothata ba ho robala (vivid dreams or difficulty sleeping).

english_text: Report any unusual symptoms to your healthcare provider as soon as possible.
sesotho_text: Tlaleha matšoao afe kapa afe a sa tloaelehang ho mofani oa hau oa litšebeletso tsa bophelo (healthcare provider) kapele kamoo ho ka khonehang.

english_text: Do not stop taking your ART without speaking to your doctor even if you have side effects.
sesotho_text: U se ke ua tlohela ho nka phekolo ea hau ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ntle le ho bua le ngaka ea hau, leha eba u e-na le liphello tsa lehlakore (side effects).

english_text: Most side effects of ART improve after the first few weeks of treatment.
sesotho_text: Liphello tse ngata tsa lehlakore tsa ART lia ntlafala ka mor'a libeke tse seng kae tsa pele tsa phekolo.

english_text: Some HIV medicines can cause changes in body fat distribution.
sesotho_text: Meriana e meng ea HIV e ka baka liphetoho tseleng eo mafura a mmele a ikarolang ka eona (changes in body fat distribution).

english_text: Long-term ART use can affect bone density and your doctor may recommend calcium supplements.
sesotho_text: Tšebeliso ea nako e telele ea ART e ka ama boima ba masapo (bone density), 'me ngaka ea hau e ka khothaletsa hore u nke li-supplement tsa k'halsiamo (calcium supplements).

english_text: Some ART medicines can affect kidney function and regular kidney tests may be needed.
sesotho_text: Meriana e meng ea ART e ka ama tšebetso ea liphio (kidney function), 'me ho ka hlokahala hore u etse litlhahlobo tsa kamehla tsa liphio (regular kidney tests).

english_text: Peripheral neuropathy causing numbness or tingling in the hands and feet can be a side effect of some HIV medicines.
sesotho_text: Bohloko ba methapo ea kutlo (peripheral neuropathy) bo bakang ho shoa litho kapa ho hlohlona matsohong le maotong (numbness or tingling in the hands and feet) e ka ba phello ea lehlakore ea meriana e meng ea HIV.

english_text: Your doctor can switch your ART regimen if side effects are affecting your quality of life.
sesotho_text: Ngaka ea hau e ka fetola mofuta oa phekolo ea hau ea lithibela-mafofore (ART regimen) haeba liphello tsa lehlakore li ama boleng ba bophelo ba hau.

english_text: HIV can develop resistance to medicines if doses are missed regularly.
sesotho_text: Sefanjana sa HIV se ka ba le manganga khahlanong le meriana (develop resistance) haeba u lula u tlola kapa u fetwa ke nako ea ho e nka khafetsa.

english_text: Drug-resistant HIV is harder to treat and may require different medicines.
sesotho_text: Sefanjana sa HIV se seng le manganga khahlanong le meriana (drug-resistant HIV) se thata le ho feta ho se phekola, 'me se ka hloka meriana e fapaneng.

english_text: A resistance test can show which HIV medicines will still work for you.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea manganga a tšusumetso ea meriana (resistance test) e ka bontša hore na ke meriana efe ea HIV e tla tsoela pele ho u berekela.

english_text: Taking your ART correctly every day is the best way to prevent drug resistance.
sesotho_text: Ho nka phekolo ea hau ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ka nepo letsatsi le leng le le leng ke tsela e molemohali ea ho thibela manganga a tšusumetso ea meriana (prevent drug resistance).

english_text: If your viral load remains high on ART your doctor may test for drug resistance.
sesotho_text: Haeba boemo ba vaerase maling a hau (viral load) bo lula bo phahame leha u le ho ART, ngaka ea hau e ka etsa tlhahlobo ea manganga a tšusumetso ea meriana (drug resistance test).

english_text: Second-line ART is used when the first regimen stops working.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea bobeli ea lithibela-mafofore (second-line ART) e sebelisoa ha mofuta oa pele oa phekolo (first regimen) o khaotsa ho bereka.

english_text: Third-line ART is reserved for people with resistance to multiple HIV medicines.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea boraro ea lithibela-mafofore (third-line ART) e bolokeloa batho ba nang le manganga khahlanong le meriana e mengata ea HIV (resistance to multiple HIV medicines).

english_text: Sharing HIV medicines with others can lead to drug resistance.
sesotho_text: Ho abelana meriana ea HIV le batho ba bang ho ka baka hore sefanjana se be le manganga khahlanong le meriana (drug resistance).

english_text: Alcohol and drug use can make it harder to take ART consistently.
sesotho_text: Tšebeliso ea joala le lithethefatsi e ka etsa hore ho be thata le ho feta ho nka phekolo ea hau ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ka linako tsohle le ka tsela e nepahetseng (take ART consistently).

english_text: Mental health problems can make it difficult to adhere to ART.
sesotho_text: Mathata a bophelo ba kelello (mental health problems) a ka etsa hore ho be thata ho khomarela le ho nka phekolo ea hau ea lithibela-mafofore ka nepo (adhere to ART).

english_text: Children living with HIV need ART in doses appropriate for their age and weight.
sesotho_text: Bana ba phelang le HIV ba hloka phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ka litekanyetso tse nepahetseng bakeng sa lilemo le boima ba bona ba mmele (appropriate for their age and weight).

english_text: Adolescents living with HIV face unique challenges in staying on treatment.
sesotho_text: Bacha ba phelang le HIV ba tobana le liatleho le mathata a ikhethang (unique challenges) tabeng ea ho lula ba le phekong le ho nka meriana ea bona khafetsa (staying on treatment).

english_text: Older adults living with HIV may need extra monitoring for other health conditions.
sesotho_text: Batho ba hotseng ba phelang le HIV ba ka hloka tlhahlobo le tlhokomelo e eketsehileng (extra monitoring) bakeng sa maemo a mang a bophelo kapa mafu a mang.

english_text: Pregnant women on ART should continue their treatment throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding.
sesotho_text: Bo-mme ba bakhachane ba leng ho phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ba lokela ho tsoela pele ka meriana ea bona nakong eohle ea bokhachane le ha ba tsoela pele ho nyantša.

english_text: HIV-positive mothers on ART can breastfeed safely if they maintain an undetectable viral load.
sesotho_text: Bo-mme ba phelang le HIV ba leng ho phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ba ka nyantša ka mokhoa o nang le tšireletseho (breastfeed safely) haeba ba lula ba e-na le boemo ba vaerase bo ke keng ba bonahala maling (maintain an undetectable viral load).

english_text: People who inject drugs living with HIV should receive ART alongside addiction treatment.
sesotho_text: Batho ba hlabang ka lithethefatsi (people who inject drugs) ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho fumana phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) mmoho le phekolo ea ho tlohela bokhoba ba lino le lithethefatsi (addiction treatment).

english_text: Sex workers living with HIV have the same right to ART as all other people.
sesotho_text: Batho ba rekisang ka mmele ba phelang le HIV ba na le tokelo e tšoanang ea ho fumana phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) joaloka batho ba bang bohle.

english_text: Prisoners living with HIV must have access to ART while in detention.
sesotho_text: Batšoaruoa ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho ba le monyetla oa ho fumana phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) ka hara literonko nakong eo ba tšoeroeng (while in detention).

english_text: Transgender people living with HIV should receive ART and gender-affirming care together.
sesotho_text: Batho ba fetotseng bong (transgender people) ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho fumana phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) mmoho le tlhokomelo e tiisang bong ba bona (gender-affirming care).

english_text: People with TB and HIV should start TB treatment first and then begin ART as soon as possible.
sesotho_text: Batho ba nang le lefuba (TB) le HIV ba lokela ho qala ka phekolo ea lefuba pele, ebe ba qala phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) kapele kamoo ho ka khonehang (as soon as possible).

english_text: Opportunistic infections take advantage of a weakened immune system in people with HIV.
sesotho_text: Mafu a tlatsetso (opportunistic infections) a nka monyetla ka bofokoli ba masole a mmele (weakened immune system) ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Pneumocystis pneumonia is a serious lung infection that can occur in people with low CD4 counts.
sesotho_text: Lefu la matšofong la Pneumocystis pneumonia ke tšoaetso e mpe haholo ea matšofong e ka hlahang ho batho ba nang le lipalo tse tlase tsa masole a mmele a CD4 (low CD4 counts).

english_text: Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis prevents certain infections in people with low CD4 counts.
sesotho_text: Tšebeliso ea moriana oa Cotrimoxazole e le tšireletso (Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis) e thibela lits'oetso tse itseng ho batho ba nang le lipalo tse tlase tsa masole a mmele a CD4 (low CD4 counts).

english_text: Cryptococcal meningitis is a life-threatening fungal infection that affects people with advanced HIV.
sesotho_text: Cryptococcal meningitis ke tšoaetso e kotsi haholo ea fungal e behang bophelo kotsing (life-threatening fungal infection) e amang batho ba nang le boemo bo tsoetseng pele ba HIV (advanced HIV).

english_text: Toxoplasmosis can cause brain disease in people with severely weakened immune systems.
sesotho_text: Toxoplasmosis e ka baka lefu la boko (brain disease) ho batho ba nang le masole a mmele a fokolang haholo (severely weakened immune systems).

english_text: Candidiasis or thrush is a common fungal infection in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Candidiasis kapa molomo o mofubelu (thrush) ke tšoaetso e tloaelehileng ea fungal (common fungal infection) ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Cytomegalovirus can cause blindness in people with very low CD4 counts.
sesotho_text: Cytomegalovirus e ka baka bofofu (blindness) ho batho ba nang le lipalo tse tlase haholo tsa masole a mmele a CD4 (very low CD4 counts).

english_text: Kaposi sarcoma is a cancer that can develop in people with advanced HIV disease.
sesotho_text: Kaposi sarcoma ke kankere e ka hlahang ho batho ba nang le boemo bo tsoetseng pele ba lefu la HIV (advanced HIV disease).

english_text: ART prevents opportunistic infections by restoring the immune system.
sesotho_text: Phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) e thibela mafu a tlatsetso (opportunistic infections) ka ho tsosolosa le ho matlafatsa masole a mmele (restoring the immune system).

english_text: People with HIV should receive vaccinations to prevent certain opportunistic infections.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho fumana liente (vaccinations) ho thibela mafu a itseng a tlatsetso (certain opportunistic infections)

english_text: Good nutrition supports the immune system and helps ART work effectively.
sesotho_text: Phepo e ntle ea ’mele e tšehetsa masole a ’mele (immune system) hape e thusa hore phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) e sebetse ka mokhoa o nang le katleho.

english_text: People living with HIV should eat a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho ja lijo tse nang le phepo e leka-lekaneng (balanced diet) tse nang le litholoana le meroho e mengata.

english_text: Protein-rich foods help repair body tissues and support immune function in people with HIV.
sesotho_text: Lijo tse nang le protheine e ngata (protein-rich foods) li baka hore mmele o khone ho lokisa lisele tse senyehileng (repair body tissues) hape li tšehetsa tšebetso ea masole a mmele (immune function) ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Avoid eating raw or undercooked food if your immune system is weakened by HIV.
sesotho_text: Qoba ho ja lijo tse sa butsoang hantle kapa tse tala (raw or undercooked food) haeba masole a hau a ’mele a fokolitsoe ke HIV (weakened immune system).

english_text: Drink only safe clean water to avoid waterborne infections.
sesotho_text: Inua feela metsi a bolokehileng le a hloekileng (safe clean water) ho qoba lits'oetso tse tsamaisang ka metsi (waterborne infections).

english_text: Alcohol can interfere with ART and weaken your immune system.
sesotho_text: Joala bo ka kena-kenana le phekolo ea lithibela-mafofore (ART) hape bo ka fokolisa masole a hau a ’mele (weaken your immune system).

english_text: Smoking increases the risk of lung infections and cancers in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho tsuba ho eketsa kotsi ea lits'oetso tsa matšoafo (lung infections) le likankere (cancers) ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Regular exercise can improve energy levels and mental health in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho ikoetlisa kamehla (regular exercise) ho ka ntlafatsa maemo a matla (energy levels) le bophelo bo botle ba kelello (mental health) ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Adequate sleep helps the immune system function properly.
sesotho_text: Boroko bo lekaneng bo thusa masole a ’mele (immune system) hore a sebetse ka mokhoa o nepahetseng (function properly).

english_text: Stress management is important for people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Stress management is very important for people living with HIV.

english_text: HIV stigma can prevent people from getting tested and starting treatment.
sesotho_text: Khethollo e amanang le HIV (HIV stigma) e ka thibela batho ho e-ea ho hlahlojoa (getting tested) le ho qala phekolo (starting treatment).

english_text: People living with HIV deserve to be treated with dignity and respect.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho tšoaroa ka seriti le tlhompho (dignity and respect).

english_text: Discrimination against people living with HIV is a violation of human rights.
sesotho_text: Khethollo khahlanong le batho ba phelang le HIV ke tlolo ea litokelo tsa botho (violation of human rights).

english_text: Disclosing your HIV status to a trusted person can provide emotional support.
sesotho_text: Ho bolella motho eo u mo tšepang ka boemo ba hau ba HIV ho ka u fa tšehetso e matla ea maikutlo.

english_text: You are not required by law to disclose your HIV status to your employer.
sesotho_text: Ha u tlamelloe ke molao ho bolella mookameli oa hau oa mosebetsi ka boemo ba hau ba HIV.

english_text: Support groups for people living with HIV can help reduce feelings of isolation.
sesotho_text: Lihlopha tsa tšehetso bakeng sa batho ba phelang le HIV li ka thusa ho fokotsa maikutlo a ho ikutloa u le mong.

english_text: Counselling can help people living with HIV cope with emotional challenges.
sesotho_text: Therollo ea maikutlo e ka bophelo e ka thusa batho ba phelang le HIV ho mamella le ho hlola mathata a maikutlo.

english_text: Children should be told about their HIV status in an age-appropriate way.
sesotho_text: Bana ba lokela ho bolelloa ka boemo ba bona ba HIV ka mokhoa o lumellanang le lilemo tsa bona.

english_text: Community health workers play an important role in supporting people on ART.
sesotho_text: Basebeletsi ba bophelo bo botle ba sechaba ba na le karolo e bohlokoa haholo eo ba e bapalang ho tšehetsa batho ba ntseng ba nka liphekolo tsa ART.

english_text: Peer support from other people living with HIV can improve treatment adherence.
sesotho_text: Tšehetso e tsoang ho batho ba bang ba phelang le HIV e ka thusa ho ntlafatsa mokhoa oa ho nka meriana ka nepo.

english_text: Using a condom correctly every time you have sex reduces the risk of HIV transmission.
sesotho_text: Ho sebelisa khondomo ka nepo nako le nako ha u kopanela liphate ho fokotsa kotsi ea ho fetisa HIV.

english_text: Pre-exposure prophylaxis is a daily medicine that prevents HIV in people at high risk.
sesotho_text: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) ke moriana o nkoang letsatsi le letsatsi o thibelang HIV ho batho ba kotsing e phahameng ea ho tšoaetsoa.

english_text: Post-exposure prophylaxis must be started within 72 hours of a possible HIV exposure.
sesotho_text: Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) e lokela ho qaloa ka hare ho lihora tse 72 ka mor'a hore motho a ka ba a pepesitsoe kotsing ea HIV.

english_text: HIV cannot be transmitted through hugging, shaking hands, or sharing food.
sesotho_text: HIV e ke ke ea phetisoa ka ho kopa, ho tšoarana ka matsoho kapa ho abelana lijo.

english_text: HIV is transmitted through blood, breast milk, semen, and vaginal fluids.
sesotho_text: HIV e fetisoa ka mali, lebese la letsoele, marere a banna, le lino-mapholi tsa botšehali.

english_text: Needle exchange programmes reduce HIV transmission among people who inject drugs.
sesotho_text: Mananeo a ho fapanyetsana linale a fokotsa phetiso ea HIV har'a batho ba itlhahisang meriana kapa lithethefatsi ka linale.

english_text: Voluntary medical male circumcision reduces the risk of HIV in men.
sesotho_text: Ho circumcision kapa ho koba banna ka boithatelo ho fokotsa kotsi ea ho tšoaetsoa ke HIV ho banna.

english_text: Blood donations are screened for HIV to protect recipients.
sesotho_text: Mali a fanoang a hlahlobeloa HIV ho sireletsa batho ba a amohelang.

english_text: Knowing your HIV status is the first step in protecting yourself and others.
sesotho_text: Ho tseba boemo ba hau ba HIV ke mohato oa pele oa ho itšireletsa le ho sireletsa ba bang.

english_text: HIV testing should be offered routinely at all health facilities.
sesotho_text: Liteko tsa HIV li lokela ho fanoa kamehla litsing tsohle tsa bophelo bo botle.

english_text: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission programmes save thousands of babies from HIV every year.
sesotho_text: Mananeo a ho thibela phetiso ea HIV ho tloha ho 'm'e ho ea ho ngoana a pholosa masea a likete selemo le selemo.

english_text: All pregnant women should be tested for HIV at their first antenatal visit.
sesotho_text: Basali bohle ba bakhachane ba lokela ho hlahlobeloa HIV leetong la bona la pele la ho ea kliniki.

english_text: HIV-positive pregnant women must start ART immediately to protect their baby.
sesotho_text: Basali ba bakhachane ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho qala ART hang-hang ho sireletsa masea a bona.

english_text: Without treatment the risk of a mother passing HIV to her baby is up to 45 percent.
sesotho_text: Kantle le kalafo, kotsi ea hore 'm'e a fetisetse HIV ho ngoana oa hae e ka ba ho fihla ho liperesente tse 45 (45%).

english_text: With effective ART the risk of mother-to-child HIV transmission can be reduced to less than one percent.
sesotho_text: Ka kalafo e sebetsang ea ART, kotsi ea hore 'm'e a fetisetse HIV ho ngoana oa hae e ka fokotsoa ho ba ka tlase ho liperesente tse le 'ngoe (1%).

english_text: Babies born to HIV-positive mothers should receive nevirapine syrup after birth.
sesotho_text: Masea a hlahileng ho bo-'m'e ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho fuoa sirapo ea nevirapine ka mor'a ho tsoaloa.

english_text: All babies born to HIV-positive mothers should be tested for HIV at six weeks of age.
sesotho_text: Masea ohle a hlahileng ho bo-'m'e ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho hlahlobeloa HIV ha ba le libeke tse tšeletseng.

english_text: HIV-positive mothers should continue ART after delivery to protect their own health.
sesotho_text: Bo-'m'e ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho tsoela pele ka ART ka mor'a ho beleha ho sireletsa bophelo ba bona.

english_text: Formula feeding is an alternative for HIV-positive mothers who cannot safely breastfeed.
sesotho_text: Ho fepa masea ka lebese la moroetsana (formula) ke khetho e 'ngoe bakeng sa bo-'m'e ba phelang le HIV ba sa khoneng ho anyesa ka mokhoa o bolokehileng.

english_text: Mixed feeding of breast milk and formula increases the risk of HIV transmission to the baby.
sesotho_text: Ho fepa ngoana ka ho kopanya lebese la 'm'e le la moroetsana (formula) ho eketsa kotsi ea ho fetisetsa HIV ho ngoana.

english_text: TB is the leading cause of death among people living with HIV worldwide.
sesotho_text: Lefuba (TB) ke lona le bakang mafu a mangata ka ho fetisisa har'a batho ba phelang le HIV lefatšeng ka bophara.

english_text: People living with HIV are twenty times more likely to develop active TB.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba na le monyetla o phahameng ka makhetlo a mashome a mabeli (20) oa ho tšoaroa ke lefu la lefuba le tšoaetsanang (active TB).

english_text: All people living with HIV should be screened for TB at every clinic visit.
sesotho_text: Batho bohle ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho hlahlobeloa lefuba (TB) leetong le leng le le leng la bona la ho ea kliniki.

english_text: TB preventive therapy should be given to all people living with HIV who do not have active TB.
sesotho_text: Kalafo e thibelang lefuba (TB preventive therapy) e lokela ho fuoa batho bohle ba phelang le HIV ba se nang lefu la lefuba le tšoaetsanang (active TB).

english_text: HIV-positive people with TB must take both TB medicines and ART at the same time.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba nang le lefuba (TB) ba lokela ho nka meriana ea TB le ea ART ka nako e le 'ngoe.

english_text: Drug interactions between TB medicines and ART must be carefully managed.
sesotho_text: Likamano pakeng tsa meriana ea lefuba (TB) le ea ART li lokela ho tsamaisoa ka hloko e kholo ho qoba lits'enyehelo kapa ho fokotsa matla a tsona.

english_text: Rifampicin used in TB treatment can reduce the effectiveness of some ART medicines.
sesotho_text: Rifampicin e sebelisoang kalafong ea lefuba (TB) e ka fokotsa matla a meriana e meng ea ART.

english_text: Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome can occur when ART is started in people with TB.
sesotho_text: Lebitso la lefu la ho ruruha ha mmele ha o qala ART (Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome - IRIS) le ka hlaha ha motho ea nang le lefuba (TB) a qala kalafo ea ART.

english_text: People with HIV and TB need close monitoring and regular clinic visits.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV le lefu la lefuba (TB) ba hloka tlhokomelo e haufi le ho etela kliniki kamehla.

english_text: Treating both HIV and TB together saves lives and reduces transmission of both diseases.
sesotho_text: Ho phekola HIV le lefu la lefuba (TB) ka nako e le 'ngoe ho pholosa bophelo mme ho fokotsa ho tšoaetsana ha mafu ana ka bobeli.

english_text: HIV testing is confidential and your results cannot be shared without your consent.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea HIV ke ntho ea sephiri mme liphetho tsa hau li ke ke tsa arolelanoa le batho ba bang ntle le tumello ea hau.

english_text: Rapid HIV tests can give results within 20 minutes.
sesotho_text: Litlhahlobo tse potlakileng tsa HIV (rapid HIV tests) li ka fana ka liphetho ka tlase ho metsotso e mashome a mabeli (20).

english_text: A positive HIV test result should always be confirmed with a second test.
sesotho_text: Liphetho tse bontšang hore u na le HIV (positive HIV test result) li lokela ho netefatsoa ka tlhahlobo ea bobeli kamehla.

english_text: HIV self-testing kits allow people to test themselves in private.
sesotho_text: Lisebelisoa tsa ho itlhahloba HIV (HIV self-testing kits) li lumella batho ho itlhahloba ba le boeena le lekunutung.

english_text: A negative HIV test result means you did not have HIV at the time of testing.
sesotho_text: Liphetho tse bontšang hore ha u na HIV (negative HIV test result) li bolela hore u ne u se na HIV ka nako eo u neng u hlahlobjoa ka eona.

english_text: The window period is the time between HIV infection and when a test can detect the virus.
sesotho_text: Nako ea fensetere (window period) ke nako e pakeng tsa ha motho a tšoaetsoa ke HIV le nako eo tlhahlobo e khonang ho lemoha vaerase eo ka mmele.

english_text: Testing again after the window period gives a more accurate result.
sesotho_text: Ho ikemisetsa ho hlahlobjoa hape ka mor'a hore nako ea fensetere (window period) e fete ho fana ka liphetho tse nepahetseng le ho feta.

english_text: Couples should test for HIV together to support each other.
sesotho_text: Banyalani kapa baratani ba lokela ho hlahlobeloa HIV hammoho ho tšehetsana le ho ba matla mmoho.

english_text: Provider-initiated HIV testing should be offered at all health facilities.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea HIV e qaloang ke mofani oa lits'ebeletso tsa bophelo (provider-initiated HIV testing) e lokela ho fanoa litsing tsohle tsa bophelo.

english_text: Community-based HIV testing reaches people who do not visit health facilities.
sesotho_text: Tlhahlobo ea HIV e fanoang metseng (community-based HIV testing) e fihlela batho ba sa eteleng litsi tsa bophelo.

english_text: Depression is common in people living with HIV and should be treated.
sesotho_text: Ho tepella maikutlong (depression) ho tloaelehile ho batho ba phelang le HIV mme ho lokela ho phekoloa.

english_text: Anxiety about HIV status and treatment can affect daily life and adherence.
sesotho_text: Ho tšoenyeha kapa ho ba le matšoenyeho (anxiety) ka boemo ba hau ba HIV le kalafo ho ka ama bophelo ba hau ba letsatsi le letsatsi le mokhoa oo u neng u tla nka meriana ka oona ka nepo.

english_text: Mental health support should be integrated into HIV care.
sesotho_text: Tšehetso ea bophelo bo botle ba kelello (mental health support) e lokela ho kenyeletsoa le ho loantšoa mmoho le tlhokomelo ea HIV.

english_text: People living with HIV who have mental health problems are less likely to stay on treatment.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba nang le mathata a bophelo bo botle ba kelello ba na le monyetla o fokolang oa ho tsoela pele kapa ho khomarela kalafo ea bona.

english_text: Counselling and psychosocial support improve quality of life for people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Therapo ea kelello (counseling) le tšehetso ea maikutlo le loago (psychosocial support) li ntlafatsa boleng ba bophelo ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: HIV-related grief and loss can cause prolonged sadness that requires professional support.
sesotho_text: Mahlomola le tahlehelo tse amanang le HIV li ka baka masoabi a nako e telele a hlokang tšehetso le thuso ea litsebi tsa bophelo bo botle ba kelello.

english_text: Substance use disorders are more common in people living with HIV and need to be addressed.
sesotho_text: Mafu a tšebeliso e mpe ea lino kapa lithethefatsi (substance use disorders) a tloaelehile haholo ho batho ba phelang le HIV mme ho hlokahala hore ho sebetsanoe le ona ka tieo.

english_text: Post-traumatic stress disorder is more common in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Lefu la khatello ea maikutlo ka mor'a ho traumatic (post-traumatic stress disorder - PTSD) le tloaelehile haholo ho batho ba phelang le HIV mme le hloka tlhokomelo e khethehileng.

english_text: Integrated mental health and HIV care leads to better treatment outcomes.
sesotho_text: Tlhokomelo e kopantseng bophelo bo botle ba kelello le ea HIV (integrated mental health and HIV care) e isa ho liphetho tse betere haholo tsa kalafo.

english_text: People living with HIV should be screened for depression at every clinic visit.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho hlahlobeloa ho tepella maikutlong (depression) nako le nako ha ba etetse litleliniki.

english_text: Micronutrient deficiencies are common in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho hlokahala ha limatlafatsi tse nyane (micronutrient deficiencies) ho tloaelehile ho batho ba phelang le HIV mme ho bohlokoa hore li hlokomeloe.

english_text: Zinc deficiency can worsen immune function in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho hlokahala ha sinki (zinc deficiency) ho ka mpefatsa tšebetso ea sesole sa mmele ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Vitamin B12 deficiency is common in people taking certain ART medicines.
sesotho_text: Ho hlokahala ha vithamine B12 (vitamin B12 deficiency) ho tloaelehile ho batho ba nkang meriana e itseng ea mofuta oa ART.

english_text: People living with HIV have higher energy needs especially when they are ill.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba na le tlhoko e phahameng ea matla (energy needs), haholo-holo ha ba kula.

english_text: Food insecurity can make it harder for people living with HIV to take their medicines.
sesotho_text: Ho hloka ts'ireletso ea lijo (food insecurity) ho ka etsa hore ho be boima haholo ho batho ba phelang le HIV ho nka meriana ea bona ka nepo.

english_text: Nutrition support programmes can improve ART adherence and treatment outcomes.
sesotho_text: Mananeo a tšehetso ea phepo e nepahetseng (nutrition support programmes) a ka ntlafatsa mokhoa oa ho khomarela meriana ea ART hammoho le liphetho tse betere tsa kalafo.

english_text: Weight loss in people living with HIV can be a sign of treatment failure or opportunistic infection.
sesotho_text: Ho theoha ha boima ba mmele ho batho ba phelang le HIV ho ka ba sesupo sa ho hloleha hoa kalafo (treatment failure) kapa ho hlaseloa ke mafu a mpefalang ka lebaka la bofokoli ba sesole sa mmele (opportunistic infection).

english_text: Diarrhoea caused by HIV or ART can lead to malnutrition if not managed.
sesotho_text: Letshollo le bakiloeng ke HIV kapa meriana ea ART le ka baka phepo e mpe (malnutrition) ha le sa laoloe kapa la phekoloa ka nako.

english_text: Herbal remedies and traditional medicines can interact with ART.
sesotho_text: Litlhare tsa litlama le meriana ea setso (herbal remedies and traditional medicines) li ka thulana kapa tsa kena-kenana le tšebetso ea meriana ea ART (interact with ART).

english_text: Always tell your healthcare provider about any traditional or herbal medicines you are taking.
sesotho_text: Kamehla bolella mofani oa hau oa tlhokomelo ea bophelo bo botle ka meriana efe kapa efe ea setso kapa ea litlama eo u e nkang.

english_text: People living with HIV are at higher risk of cardiovascular disease.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba kotsing e phahameng haholo ea ho tšoaroa ke mafu a pelo le methapo ea mali (cardiovascular disease).

english_text: Regular blood pressure and cholesterol checks are important for people on long-term ART.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahloba khatello ea mali (blood pressure) le kiroseterolo (cholesterol) khafetsa ho bohlokoa haholo ho batho ba ntseng ba nka meriana ea ART ka nako e telele.

english_text: People living with HIV have a higher risk of certain cancers.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba kotsing e phahameng haholo ea ho tšoaroa ke mefuta e itseng ea kankere (certain cancers).

english_text: Cervical cancer screening is especially important for women living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho hlahlobela kankere ea molomo oa popelo (cervical cancer screening) ho bohlokoa haholo ho basali ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: People living with HIV should have regular dental check-ups.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho hlahlobana le ngaka ea meno khafetsa (regular dental check-ups).

english_text: Oral health problems such as thrush and gum disease are common in people with HIV.
sesotho_text: Mathata a bophelo bo botle ba molomo, a kang tšea (thrush) le lefu la marinini (gum disease), a tloaelehile ho batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: Bone density loss is a long-term concern for people on ART.
sesotho_text: Ho lahleheloa ke letsetse la masapo (bone density loss) ke ntho e tšoenyang ka nako e telele ho batho ba ntseng ba nka meriana ea ART.

english_text: People living with HIV should avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen.
sesotho_text: Batho ba phelang le HIV ba lokela ho qoba ho lula letsatsing nako e telele mme ba sebelise setlolo se thibelang kotsi ea mahlaseli a letsatsi (sunscreen).

english_text: Kidney function should be monitored regularly in people taking tenofovir-based ART.
sesotho_text: Tšebetso ea liphio (kidney function) e lokela ho hlahlojoa khafetsa ho batho ba ntseng ba nka meriana ea ART e nang le tenofovir (tenofovir-based ART).

english_text: Liver disease is a significant cause of illness in people living with HIV.
sesotho_text: Lefu la sebete (liver disease) ke sesupo le se baki se seholo sa ho kula har'a batho ba phelang le HIV.

english_text: I was told I have HIV and I do not know where to start.
sesotho_text: Ke bolelletsoe hore ke na le HIV 'me ha ke tsebe hore na ke qale kae.

english_text: I am scared to start taking HIV medicines.
sesotho_text: Ke tšohile ho qala ho nka meriana ea HIV.

english_text: I have been taking my HIV medicines for one month and I feel much better.
sesotho_text: Ke qetile khoeli ke nka meriana ea ka ea HIV 'me ke ikutloa ke le betere haholo.

english_text: I forgot to take my HIV medicine yesterday and I am worried.
sesotho_text: Ke lebetse ho nka moriana oa ka oa HIV maobane 'me ke tšoenyehile.

english_text: My HIV medicine makes me feel dizzy in the morning.
sesotho_text: Meriana ea ka ea HIV e nts'ebisa ditaemane hoseng.

english_text: I do not want my family to know that I am taking HIV medicine.
sesotho_text: Ha ke batle hore lelapa la ka le tsebe hore ke nka meriana ea HIV.

english_text: I am pregnant and I just found out I have HIV.
sesotho_text: Ke mmele o rona mme ke sa tsoa fumana hore ke na le HIV.

english_text: I want to know if my baby has HIV.
sesotho_text: Ke batla ho tseba hore na ngoana oa ka o na le HIV.

english_text: I have been on HIV treatment for five years and my viral load is undetectable.
sesotho_text: Ke bile kalafong ea HIV lilemo tse hlano mme vaerale loute (viral load) ea ka ha e sa bonahala.

english_text: I stopped taking my HIV medicine because I felt healthy and now I am sick again.
sesotho_text: Ke ile ka emisa ho nka meriana ea ka ea HIV hobane ke ne ke ikutloa ke phetse hantle, mme hona joale ke se ke kula hape.

english_text: HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system.
sesotho_text: HIV ke vaerase e hlaselang sesole sa mmele.

english_text: HIV stands for Human Immunodeficiency Virus.
sesotho_text: HIV e emela Human Immunodeficiency Virus.

english_text: AIDS stands for Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome.
sesotho_text: AIDS e emela Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome.

english_text: AIDS is the most advanced stage of HIV infection.
sesotho_text: AIDS ke mohato o tsoetseng pele haholo oa tšoaetso ea HIV.

english_text: Not everyone with HIV develops AIDS especially if they are on treatment.
sesotho_text: Ha se motho e mong le e mong ea nang le HIV ea bang le AIDS, haholo-holo haeba a le kalafong.

english_text: HIV is transmitted through contact with infected blood, semen, vaginal fluids, rectal fluids, or breast milk.
sesotho_text: HIV e fetisoa ka ho kopana le mali a tšoaelitsoeng, peleu, lero la botšehali, lero la rectum, kapa lebese la letsoele.

english_text: HIV cannot survive for long outside the human body.
sesotho_text: HIV e ke ke ea phela nako e telele kantle ho 'mele oa motho.

english_text: You cannot get HIV from mosquito bites.
sesotho_text: U ke ke ua tšoaroa ke HIV ka lebaka la ho llongwa ke menoang.

english_text: You cannot get HIV from toilet seats or swimming pools.
sesotho_text: U ke ke ua tšoaroa ke HIV ka lebaka la litulo tsa matloana kapa liliba tsa ho tola (swimming pools).

english_text: You cannot get HIV from saliva, tears, or sweat.
sesotho_text: U ke ke ua tšoaroa ke HIV ka lebaka la mathe, meokho, kapa mofufutso.

english_text: Unprotected sex with an HIV-positive partner is the most common way HIV is transmitted.
sesotho_text: Ho kopana thobalano ho sa sireletsehang le molekane ea nang le HIV ke eona tsela e tloaelehileng haholo eo HIV e fetisoang ka eona.

english_text: Sharing needles or syringes with someone who has HIV can transmit the virus.
sesotho_text: Ho abelana ka linalete kapa lisirinji le motho ea nang le HIV ho ka fetisa vaerase.

english_text: HIV can be passed from a mother to her baby during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding.
sesotho_text: HIV e ka fetisoa ho tloha ho 'm'e ho ea ho lesea la hae nakong ea bokhachane, pelehi, kapa ha a anyesa.

english_text: Receiving a blood transfusion with HIV-infected blood can transmit the virus.
sesotho_text: Ho tšeloa mali a nang le tšoaetso ea HIV ho ka fetisa vaerase.

english_text: Healthcare workers can be exposed to HIV through needlestick injuries.
sesotho_text: Basebeletsi ba tsa bophelo bo itekanetseng ba ka ba kotsing ea ho tšoaroa ke HIV ka lebaka la ho hlaboa ke linalete ka phoso.

english_text: Abstaining from sex is the most effective way to prevent sexual transmission of HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho ikaba thobalano ke eona tsela e sebetsang ka ho fetisisa ea ho thibela phetiso ea HIV ka thobalano.

english_text: Being in a mutually faithful relationship with an HIV-negative partner reduces the risk of HIV.
sesotho_text: Ho ba kamanong e tšepahalang le molekane ea se nang HIV ho fokotsa kotsi ea ho tšoaroa ke HIV.

english_text: Male condoms reduce the risk of HIV transmission by more than 90 percent when used correctly.
sesotho_text: Likhohlopo tsa banna li fokotsa kotsi ea phetiso ea HIV ka liphesente tse fetang 90 ha li sebelisoa ka nepo.

english_text: Female condoms are also effective at preventing HIV when used correctly.
sesotho_text: Likhohlopo tsa basali le tsona li sebetsa hantle ho thibela HIV ha li sebelisoa ka nepo.

english_text: Condoms must be used from the beginning to the end of every sexual encounter.
sesotho_text: Likhohlopo li lokela ho sebelisoa ho tloha qalong ho fihlela qetellong ea ketso e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe ea thobalano.
